 Trending Legal Opinion & Research Policy & Initiative ​EPFO Sees Legal Options Closed for Recovering ₹1,800 Crore from Reliance Capital
 Last updated: November 19, 2026 11:40 am 
 By 
 Rajesh Rai 
 Share 
 4 Min Read 
 SHARE 
 Follow us on Google News
 New Delhi: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), which manages retirement savings for millions of salaried workers across India, sees almost no remaining hope of recovering around ₹1,800 crore in pending dues from Reliance Capital Limited (RCL). The retirement fund body has informed its board of trustees that effective legal avenues may no longer be available to pursue additional recovery of the remaining principal and interest. The unpaid sum comprises the balance principal from its investment alongside interest admitted during the corporate insolvency resolution process.
 ​The dispute stems from investments made in 2013 and 2014, when EPFO placed ₹2,500 crore of workers’ savings into Reliance Capital debentures. Those instruments were scheduled to mature in 2023 and 2024, but the company failed to meet its repayment obligations on time, pushing the matter into insolvency proceedings. The company faced allegations of diluting assets and guarantees meant to safeguard the interests of debenture holders, including EPFO. Against a total admitted claim of ₹3,308.67 crore, comprising ₹2,500 crore in principal and ₹808.67 crore in interest, a substantial portion of employees’ funds remains unrecovered.
 ​ Nearly 60 Percent of Principal Recovered 
 ​Standard Chartered Bank, acting as custodian for Reliance Capital, informed EPFO that ₹1,492.45 crore has been received so far. This amount represents 59.70 percent of the original ₹2,500 crore principal investment, leaving ₹1,007.55 crore of the principal unpaid. Furthermore, none of the ₹808.67 crore in interest admitted under the insolvency process has been paid.
 ​Combined, the unrecovered principal and unpaid interest bring total pending dues to approximately ₹1,816 crore. In an agenda note prepared for its trustees, EPFO stated that legal counsel advised no further legal remedies remain available to recover additional funds. The note cited binding Supreme Court rulings, the resolution plan approved by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), and conditions treating the payouts received thus far as full and final settlement.
 ​ CBI Registers Case, SFIO Probe Sought 
 ​The matter is scheduled for discussion at the November 19 meeting of EPFO’s Central Board of Trustees (CBT). Alongside the recovery status, trustees will review information shared by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) detailing alleged fraudulent transactions, fund diversion, irregular loan disbursements, and other financial irregularities at the company.
 ​EPFO informed trustees that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has already registered a case in the matter. The organization has also written to the Enforcement Directorate and requested the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to refer the case to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO). A spokesperson for former Reliance Capital non-executive director and chairman Anil Ambani had earlier stated that Ambani remained on the board until November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the board and appointed an administrator, while denying any wrongdoing on his part.
 ​ Review of Other Defaulters and Fund Managers 
 ​During the meeting, the board of trustees will also review pending dues from other defaulting entities. These include around ₹85 crore in unpaid interest from the Uttar Pradesh Financial Corporation, nearly ₹5.36 crore in penal interest from Richardson and Cruddas, a ₹601.54 crore claim linked to Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services Limited, and ₹1.10 crore in overdue interest from the Punjab State Industrial Development Corporation.
 ​Additionally, trustees will evaluate the annual performance of firms managing EPFO’s investment portfolio based on a CRISIL assessment report. The review covers UTI Asset Management and SBI Funds Management, as well as exchange-traded fund managers ICICI Prudential and Nippon India Life AMC.
